messages:
sara: Quick thread for cust-aquila finetune bring-up. Merged their LoRA patch onto oak-13b-v2.1 locally and kicked a quick-eval pack. Noting a tokenizer token-id shift and an int4 oddity.
aj: Thanks — what's the merge diff look like (high level)?
sara: Small Adapter weights (~120MB), tokenizer adds 4 special tokens (<ACCT>, <AMT>, <INVC>, <DATE>). Their tokenizer.json shifts some high ids so embeddings misalign if you just splice.
kevin: Do we have their tokenizer mapping? Can we remap instead of replacing?
sara: They provided tokenizer.json. I tried two flows: 1) replace base tokenizer (works but breaks some infra assumptions), 2) map special tokens into base vocab (preferred). Mapping introduced new token ids which changed detokenization slightly.
yuki: Any runtime errors?
sara: At first yes when streaming multiple requests:
```
RuntimeError: kv_cache size mismatch: expected 16 got 12
at runtime/kv_cache.cpp:142
```
Fixed by aligning model.config.max_position_embeddings to 8192 (customer long context).
aj: Good catch. How about quality regressions?
sara: Quick eval pack results (invoice normalization / extraction):
- baseline oak-13b float16: exact_match=0.82, f1=0.89
- merged aquila-lora int4: exact_match=0.76, f1=0.86
- merged aquila-lora float16: exact_match=0.81, f1=0.88
So quantization introduced most of the drop. There's also a small detokenization difference across all variants.
kevin: Can you paste a couple of failing examples? Short ones help debug.
sara: Sure: 
```
input: "Invoice total: $1,234.56"
baseline: "Total due: $1,234.56"
merged-fp16: "Total due: $1,234.56"
merged-int4: "Total due 1234.56 dollars"
```
The int4 output removes colon and uses word form. Breaks exact matching.
aj: Looks like tokenization of "$" or the detokenizer's punctuation spacing. Try running token-level diff: `python tools/token_diff.py --ref oak13b --cand merged-int4 --input samples/invoice-quick.json`
sara: Ran token_diff; found that `$` maps to token id 2505 in base, but in mapped tokenizer it became two tokens (63, 4007). That explains spacing.
yuki: So two remediation paths: 1) force base tokenizer and re-index LoRA to base ids (hard), 2) add token remapping step in preprocess/postprocess to normalize $ -> one token for evaluation and production.
kevin: For rollout strategy, can we canary float16 variant (no quant) while we sort int4? Cost hit but keeps quality. Propose canary 5% on dedicated pool, fallback to oak-13b on regression.
aj: I'll set up canary config. Also add a regression alert threshold: EM drop >= 0.04 triggers automatic fallback.
sara: I created a quick GH issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/customer-onboards/issues/4321 — includes token diffs, sample failures, and suggested remediation steps.
kevin: Also run a quantization sim script with bias-correction for LoRA: `scripts/quant_sim.py --model merged/aquila-lora --method perchannel --calib-size 500`
sara: Kicked the sim; eval-bot posted results at 1754444400.
eval-bot: quant_sim results: int4 perchannel reduced EM by 0.05, QAT sim (fake-quant during fine-tune) projected EM loss 0.02. Details saved to /artifacts/aquila/1754444321/quant_sim.json
yuki: Good to have numbers. Suggest try per-channel symmetric vs asymmetric and check embedding remap impact independently.
kevin: Action items: (1) try token remap postprocess for $ and punctuation (sara), (2) run QAT or re-do LoRA with token-aligned merges (kevin), (3) canary float16 rollout (aj) with fallback policy, (4) add automated token-diff check to quick-eval pack (yuki).
sara: Working on (1) now. Uploaded a quick patch that normalizes currency tokens in preprocess; re-ran eval: merged-int4 (with preprocess) EM improved 0.78 -> still below threshold but better.
aj: Canary configured and started: deploy-bot reported at 1754444488. Monitoring dashboards: /console/canaries/aquila/1754444321
deploy-bot: Canary deployed: aquila-lora-fp16 -> dedicated/pool-7 (5%). Fallback policy: EM_drop>=0.04 -> revert to oak-13b.
kevin: Ok — we'll pause int4 rollout until quant sim + remap complete. Reopen when we have QAT or token-aligned LoRA. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
